No test in timestamp-contract.test.mjs exercises either branch. The Class H real-wrapper test (timestamp-contract.test.mjs:505-511) only calls `runTimestampContractCheck()` against the actual, fully-present repository tree, so it can never trigger the missing/unreadable path. The Class G robustness test (timestamp-contract.test.mjs:471-498) passes `null` file content directly into the pure `checkTimestampContract`, which only exercises the pure function's own `if (!content) continue` skip -- a different code path from the wrapper's fs-level detection. The suite's own comment at timestamp-contract.test.mjs:467-468 claims this property 'is exercised for the real tree by the real-wrapper test below', which is inaccurate given the real tree has no missing files to trigger it. Fix: add a test that points the wrapper (or an equivalent fixture) at a non-existent/unreadable watched path and asserts the `missing file:` / `could not read` finding message is produced.

The two new tests are also not duplicates of each other: missing-file (existsSync false) and unreadable-file (existsSync true, readFileSync throws EISDIR) are discriminatively different branches of the same try-catch.
